catalog_citation: Kerr, Elisabeth J. 2024. Tunen syntax and information structure. LOT Dissertation Series 676. Amsterdam: LOT (open-access PDF,https://www.lotpublications.nl/Documents/676_fulltext.pdf).
catalog_locator: sec. 4.2.6.1 'Tone inventory', pp. 77-78; sec. 4.2.7 'Loanword phonology', p. 83
catalog_quote: Tunen is a tonal language and tones play an important role in marking both lexical and grammatical contrasts. There are three tone levels on the surface: H, L, and downstepped H (↓ H, realised phonetically at a mid height). The tonal system is best analysed as having two tones underlyingly, H (high) and L (low). ... Following previous analyses (Janssens 1988; Mous 2003), I take the tone-bearing unit (TBU) to be the syllable, and nasal consonants are not taken as bearing tone, meaning that I mark tone of the syllabe on its vocalic nucleus. Tone makes both lexical and grammatical distinctions in Tunen. ... [4.2.7] Loanwords from languages with stress seem to be adopted in Tunen with H tone on the stressed syllable and low tone elsewhere, e.g. simíti ‘cement’, hɛbanána ‘banana’, ikísin ‘kitchen’. This was found across speakers in my fieldwork.

tone_statements.citation: Satre, Scott Alan; Welaze, Jacquis K; Batouan Bouyom, Joseph-Alain; Bete, Samuel; Sebineni, Alphonsine Flore. 2008. Précis d'orthographe pour la langue tunen. Yaoundé, Cameroun: Association Camerounaise pour la Traduction de la Bible et l'Alphabétisation (CABTAL). 13 pp. Manuscript, French. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 47827 (PDF attachment, 154 KB).
tone_statements.quote: Nous avons identifié 5 tons de surface en tunen : - 3 tons ponctuels, haut [á], moyen [ā] et bas [à]. - 2 tons modulés, montant [ǎ] et descendant [â]. ... nous avons découvert plusieurs paires minimales de tons pour des mots qui opposent le ton haut et le ton bas, surtout au niveau des verbes. Puisqu’il n’y a pas de paires minimales entre le ton moyen qui est rare et le ton haut, nous proposons une orthographe dans laquelle seuls les tons hauts (et les tons moyens) sont marqués par des signes diacritiques, tandis que le ton bas n’est pas marqué.
tone_statements.translation: We have identified 5 surface tones in Tunen: - 3 level tones, high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]. - 2 contour tones, rising [ǎ] and falling [â]. ... we have found several tonal minimal pairs for words that oppose high tone and low tone, especially among verbs. Since there are no minimal pairs between the mid tone, which is rare, and the high tone, we propose an orthography in which only high tones (and mid tones) are marked with diacritics, while low tone is left unmarked.
tone_statements.locator: section 3 'Les tons' (p. 6) and section 3.1 'Oppositions de tons lexicaux marquées par des signes diacritiques' (p. 7)
tone_statements.summary: Orthography guide: 5 SURFACE tones (H, M, L, rising, falling); H/L minimal pairs; mid rare; falling only in 2 words (ɛ́ɛ, bóo); grammatical tone deferred; no vowel-length contrast; nothing on stress.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding passages found verbatim in the Kerr 2024 text we hold at the stated sections and pages (4.2.6.1 pp.77-78; 4.2.7 p.83). (2) Deciding source is a 2024 fieldwork-based Leiden dissertation (LOT 676) with a phonology overview; it is recent and consistent with the held Mous 2003 Routledge chapter (sec. 2.3, two tones H/L, no stress/accent mention) and with Boyd 2015 LOT 410 (downloaded now, sec. 2.1.5, two-tone system, silent on stress). (3) not yet obtained: Dugast 1971 reference grammar (print only), Janssens 1988 and Wilkinson 1975 tone articles (print/JSTOR); all are tone-focused or older and none is known to posit word stress, so they would at most refine (e.g. an explicit 'no accent' or stem-prominence remark) rather than change 'tonal'.org); no JIPA Illustr

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 2015. The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon with a focus on vowels and vowel harmony. LOT Dissertation Series 410. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD). 413 pp.
sources.quote: 'Nen has a two-tone system underlyingly, high and low. Downstepped highs occur after an unrealised low tone before a high (Mous 2003: 286). In addition, Nen has high-tone spreading...' Four tone melodies on CVCV noun roots (L.L, L.H, H.L, H.H); verb roots lexically H, L or floating H. The only 'stress' token in the whole book is a generic checklist line (txt l.12080); nothing on stress/accent for Nen.
